html:
The Battle of Sellasia was fought in the summer of 222 BCE on the northern border of Laconia, Sparta's home territory. Macedon under King Antigonus III Doson, with the Achaean League, beat the Spartan king Cleomenes III.

Cleomenes had tried to make Sparta great again. He abolished the ephors, the officials who checked the kings, cancelled debts, shared out land and gave citizenship to many new men to rebuild the army. Then he attacked the Achaean League, the leading power in the Peloponnese, and won so often that its leader Aratus called in Macedon, Achaea's old enemy, for help.

At Sellasia the Macedonian phalanx broke the Spartan army, and most of the Spartan citizens in it were killed. Cleomenes fled to Ptolemaic Egypt, where he died a few years later. Antigonus marched into Sparta, the first time a foreign enemy had taken the city. Sparta never again counted as a great power. The young Achaean officer Philopoemen, who fought well that day, later led the league.
